propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Protector in te sperantium, Deus, sine quo nihil est validum, nihil sanctum:
multiplica super nos misericordiam tuam; ut, te rectore, te duce, sic
transeamus per bona temporalia, ut non amittamus aeterna. Per Dominum.

provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no commas round the vocative: 'Respice Domine munera' where 1962 has 'Respice, Domine, munera'; 1862 conclusion is the short cue 'Per Dominum.'; 1962 prints it out in full; the 1862 layer carries a stray glyph between sanctificatione and sumenda (line 48402 reads 'sanctiticati6ne ♦ sumenda'); it is a scan artifact, not a word, and no word is missing there; OCR defect resolved in the 1862 layer, not textual: 'sanctiticati6ne' for sanctificatione (f read as t). Corroboration: none attempted. Recorded limitation: Marked medium ONLY because of the stray diamond glyph at 48402. The words either side run straight on and nothing is missing between them, but I did not open an 1862 page image to confirm what the mark is, and I could not: the 1862's page-image artifacts are registered remote (the images tar and the facsimile PDF), and the eight tracked BookReader leaves are leaves 221, 303, 347-349 and 700-706/721-725, none of which is this page (leaf = printed folio + 85, so this page would be leaf 407). Target text is given in the project's calendar rendering: unaccented, ae/oe expanded to two letters, printed line wraps joined, and the typica's i normalised to the project's j where it occurs. The typica itself prints Iesum for Jesum. That normalisation is the project's standing practice (src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml records it in terms at lines 20439, 43595 and 43622).
